newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL-ITALY JUNE PPI, WPI SEEN STEADY MONTH/MONTH.
newsitem.headline: POLL-ITALY JUNE PPI, WPI SEEN STEADY MONTH/MONTH.

text.p: Italy's June producer and wholesale prices will remain little changed from May, but year-on-year PPI is seen edging higher because of a statistical comparison with June 1996's sharp fall, a Reuters poll of analysts showed.
National statistics institute Istat will release PPI and WPI data at 0700 GMT on Wednesday August 13.
The survey of 10 economists forecasts an average producer price (PPI) gain of 0.1 percent in June for a 1.6-percent year-on-year rise.
In May, PPI rose 0.1 percent from April and 1.1 percent year-on-year. In June 1996, PPI fell 0.4 percent but was up 0.7 percent year-on-year.

Stefano Lelli, economist at Banco di Sardegna, attributed the year-on-year rise to the statistical comparison with the monthly fall in June last year "caused by anomalous factors in the trend of energy prices."

Gianluca Sanna of Stone & McCarthy said "the recovery of the economic cycle seen in the second half is due not so much to an increase in demand, which remains flat, but rather to a rebuilding of stocks. The limited demand does not allow producers to hike prices."
June wholesale prices (WPI) are seen rising 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent year-on-year.
In May, WPI rose 0.2 percent but fell 0.2 percent year-on-year.
In June 1996, WPI fell 0.4 percent but rose 2.4 percent year-on-year.
Analysts do not see the dollar's recent strong rise contributing significantly to any price rises.

"The impact of the dollar's rise remains for the moment very limited, almost irrelevant. It's strength could cause PPI to rise a bit more, perhaps even taking it up to two percent, but this would be fairly gradual," said Francesco Giordano of CSFB.
